His Christmas recordings bring that same warmth to the festive season, with “White Christmas” providing a wonderfully nostalgic moment. Smooth vocals, a little old-school glamour and absolutely no novelty jumper required.

records.after: Taylor Swift grew from country storyteller into a global pop star, with songs including “Love Story” and “Shake It Off” inspiring enormous singalongs. Her festive repertoire includes “Santa Baby”, recorded for The Taylor Swift Holiday Collection. It’s a playful seasonal detour — even a pop superstar has a Christmas wish list.

pages.before: Taylor Alison Swift is an American singer-songwriter. One of the most popular contemporary female recording artists, she is known for narrative songs about her personal life, which has received much media attention.

records.after: Chris de Burgh has a gift for turning songs into stories, from the mysterious “Don’t Pay the Ferryman” to his romantic ballads. “A Spaceman Came Travelling” takes that storytelling somewhere rather unexpected, imagining a visitor from beyond the stars. A thoughtful Christmas tale, with a different sort of flying visitor to the usual sleigh.

pages.before:
Christopher John Davison known professionally as Chris de Burgh, is a British-Irish singer-songwriter and instrumentalist. 
He is an art rock performer who also writes pop-oriented material. 
He has had several top 40 hits in the UK and two in the US, but he is more popular in other countries, particularly Norway and Brazil.
He is most famous for his 1986 love song "The Lady in Red", which reached number one in several countries. 
De Burgh has sold over 45 million albums worldwide.

records.after: Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe brought thoughtful lyrics and electronic pop together in Pet Shop Boys, breaking through with “West End Girls”. Their seasonal contribution, “It Doesn’t Often Snow at Christmas”, keeps that dry wit intact. It’s a Christmas song with dancing shoes on and a refreshingly realistic view of the British weather.

pages.song: It Doesn't Often Snow At Christmas
pages.before: Pet Shop Boys are an English electronic pop duo, formed in London in 1981 and consisting of Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe.

records.after: Gwen Stefani first made her mark fronting No Doubt, whose “Don’t Speak” became a huge hit, before building a solo pop career. Her album You Make It Feel Like Christmas brings that distinctive voice to seasonal songs, including a title-track duet with Blake Shelton. Expect a cheerful meeting of pop energy and traditional Christmas sounds.

pages.before: Gwen Renée Stefani is an American singer, songwriter, and actress. She is a co-founder and the lead vocalist of the band No Doubt that experienced major success after their breakthrough studio album Tragic Kingdom

records.after: The Jackson 5 brought youthful energy and tightly woven harmonies to Motown, with “I Want You Back” and “ABC” introducing their sound to a huge audience. Their Christmas Album gives familiar songs the same lively treatment. On “Santa Claus Is Coming to Town”, the excitement sounds less like waiting patiently and more like counting every last minute.

records.after: John Lennon helped shape pop music with the Beatles before pursuing a solo career that included “Imagine”. Written with Yoko Ono, “Happy Xmas (War Is Over)” brings together their voices, the Plastic Ono Band and the Harlem Community Choir. Its seasonal greeting carries a serious wish for peace, making room for reflection among the celebrations.

pages.before: John Winston Ono Lennon, MBE was an English singer and songwriter who co-founded the Beatles, the most commercially successful band in the history of popular music. With fellow member Paul McCartney, he formed a celebrated songwriting partnership.

records.after: Johnny Mathis built his career on romantic ballads and a voice that makes even a familiar melody feel intimate. Christmas became an important part of his repertoire, with “When a Child Is Born” reaching the UK Christmas number one spot in 1976. It’s a gentle, hopeful performance for a quieter moment in a busy season.

pages.before: John Royce "Johnny" Mathis is an American singer of popular music and jazz. Starting his career with singles of standard music, he became highly popular as an album artist, with several dozen of his albums achieving gold or platinum status and 73 making the Billboard charts to date.

pages.before: "It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas" is a Christmas song written in 1951 by Meredith Willson. The song was originally titled "It's Beginning to Look Like Christmas". The song has been recorded by many artists. This time by Johnny.

records.after: Queen made rock music theatrical, adventurous and wonderfully singable, with Freddie Mercury’s voice at the centre of songs such as “Bohemian Rhapsody”. Their 1984 single “Thank God It’s Christmas” offers a more reflective celebration. There’s still plenty of feeling in the performance, but this time the invitation is to pause rather than stomp along.

pages.before: Queen are a British rock band that formed in London in 1970. Their classic line-up was Freddie Mercury, Brian May, Roger Taylor, and John Deacon.

records.after: Sam Ryder’s soaring voice carried “Space Man” to the Eurovision stage and helped introduce his debut album, There’s Nothing But Space, Man! His festive single “You’re Christmas to Me” swaps the cosmic setting for something closer to home. It’s an exuberant celebration of togetherness, delivered with enough enthusiasm to brighten a rather grey December afternoon.

pages.before: Sam Ryder Robinson is a British singer, songwriter, producer, composer and social media personality. He rose to prominence in 2020, after posting music covers on TikTok, during the first UK lockdown of the COVID-19 pandemic and signed to Parlophone Records.

records.after: Blossoms are the Stockport band whose self-titled debut album reached number one in 2016. Their melodic indie-pop also has a winter wardrobe: “It’s Going to Be a Cold Winter” arrived alongside “Christmas Eve (Soul Purpose)”. It’s a seasonal change of scenery for the band, with their knack for a memorable tune still firmly in place.

pages.song: Its Going To Be A Cold Winter
pages.before: Blossoms are an English indie pop band from Stockport, Greater Manchester, England. Formed in 2013, the band consists of Tom Ogden, Charlie Salt, Josh Dewhurst, Joe Donovan and Myles Kellock. They were on the BBC's Sound Of new music list for 2016 where they finished in fourth place.

records.after: Aled Jones became a familiar voice at Christmas with his 1985 recording of “Walking in the Air”, later building a career in singing and broadcasting. His hit version is separate from Peter Auty’s original performance in The Snowman. That clear, floating melody still offers a little escape from the bustle below, without anyone needing to leave the sofa.

pages.before: Aled Jones MBE is a Welsh singer best known for his television work with the BBC and ITV as well as his radio work, mainly for BBC Radio Wales and Classic FM.

records.after: Bon Jovi built their reputation on big rock choruses, with Jon Bon Jovi leading the band through hits including “Livin’ on a Prayer”. “Christmas Isn’t Christmas” takes a gentler approach, reflecting on how much the people around us matter at this time of year. It’s a heartfelt change of pace from the stadium singalongs.

pages.before: Bon Jovi, a renowned American rock band, is not typically associated with Christmas music. However, if there's a song titled "Christmas Isn't Christmas" by Bon Jovi, it might be a lesser-known or unreleased track. The band, led by Jon Bon Jovi, is famous for their rock anthems and ballads.

records.after: The Darkness brought extravagant guitar rock back into the spotlight with Permission to Land and “I Believe in a Thing Called Love”. Their festive single “Christmas Time (Don’t Let the Bells End)” applies the same larger-than-life approach to December. Subtle it isn’t, but sometimes the Christmas playlist has room for a guitar solo as well as a carol.

pages.before: The Darkness is a British rock band from Lowestoft, Suffolk, formed in 1999. The band consists of Justin Hawkins, his brother Dan Hawkins, Frankie Poullain and Rufus Taylor.

records.after: George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley made Wham! a defining pop duo of the 1980s, with hits including “Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go”. George wrote “Last Christmas”, pairing a bright melody with a bruised-hearted story. Released in 1984, it became a seasonal favourite long before finally claiming the UK Christmas number one spot in 2023.

pages.before: Wham! sparked something of a pop revival in the mid-'80s and could arguably be held responsible for sparking off the boy band trend of the '90s.

records.after: Greg Lake’s voice and musicianship were central to King Crimson and Emerson, Lake & Palmer. His solo single “I Believe in Father Christmas” brings that progressive-rock background to a thoughtful look at childhood wonder and adult expectations. Behind the grand arrangement is something more searching than a simple festive greeting, and all the more memorable for it.

pages.before: Gregory Stuart "Greg" Lake is an English singer, musician, songwriter and producer. He was a singer and bassist for King Crimson before becoming the bassist, guitarist, singer and lyricist for Emerson, Lake & Palmer.

records.after: The Spice Girls made “Wannabe” a calling card for their exuberant brand of pop, then became regular visitors to the Christmas charts. Their version of the Waitresses’ “Christmas Wrapping” appeared on the “Goodbye” single. It’s a lively seasonal side trip from a group whose songs rarely require much encouragement to get a singalong started.

pages.before: The Spice Girls are an English pop girl group formed in 1994. The group originally consisted of Melanie Brown, Melanie Chisholm, Emma Bunton, Geri Halliwell, and Victoria Beckham
The Spice Girls are an English pop girl group formed in 1994. The group originally consisted of Melanie Brown, Melanie Chisholm, Emma Bunton, Geri Halliwell, and Victoria Beckham

records.after: Kelly Clarkson and Ariana Grande each have a substantial pop career and a distinctive Christmas repertoire. They join forces on “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me”, recorded for Clarkson’s When Christmas Comes Around… album. This is a collaboration, not a new group: two expressive voices trading lines and meeting in harmonies that give the seasonal wish list extra lift.

pages.before: Kelly Clarkson and Ariana Grande got into the holiday spirit with their new single “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me”. It's so so good. Click the video link and watch them perform on Kelly's show.

records.after: The Ronettes helped define 1960s girl-group pop, with Ronnie Spector’s distinctive lead voice making “Be My Baby” instantly recognisable. Their recording of “Sleigh Ride” brings that same spirited character to Christmas. Bright harmonies and a bustling arrangement make this a lively trip through the snow, with no need to check the traffic before setting off.

pages.before: The Ronettes were an American girl group from New York City. One of the most popular groups from the 1960s, they placed nine songs on the Billboard Hot 100, five of which became Top 40 hits.

records.after: Lindsay Lohan is known for films including Mean Girls as well as a parallel career in pop music. She returned to “Jingle Bell Rock” for the soundtrack of Falling for Christmas, giving the familiar song a fresh performance. It’s a cheerful connection between her screen work and singing, with a knowing nod to an earlier movie moment.

pages.before: Lindsay Dee Lohan is an American actress and singer. Born in New York City and raised on Long Island, Lohan was signed to Ford Models at the age of three. Having appeared as a regular on the television soap opera Another World at age 10, her breakthrough came in the Walt Disney Pictures film The Parent Trap.

records.after: This Mel & Kim pairing is comedian Mel Smith and “Kids in America” singer Kim Wilde, not the Appleby sisters. They teamed up for Comic Relief’s 1987 version of “Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree”. The combination of pop vocals and comic mischief gives the old favourite a playful twist: a one-off duet with its tongue firmly in its cheek.

pages.before: A version of the song by Kim Wilde and Mel Smith (credited as "Mel & Kim" as a parody of then-popular sister act Mel and Kim), reached No. 3 on the UK Singles Chart during the Christmas 1987.

records.after: Engelbert Humperdinck made his name with romantic hits such as “Release Me” and “The Last Waltz”. His seasonal repertoire includes “Around the Christmas Tree”, from Warmest Christmas Wishes. The familiar richness of his voice suits a song centred on gathering together, offering a relaxed alternative to the more boisterous corners of the Christmas playlist.

pages.before: Engelbert Humperdinck is an English pop singer. Humperdinck has been described as "one of the finest middle-of-the-road balladeers around." His singles "Release Me" and "The Last Waltz" both topped the UK music charts in 1967, and sold more than a million copies each.

records.after: Band Aid brought together a temporary line-up of pop performers for famine relief in Ethiopia. Bob Geldof and Midge Ure wrote “Do They Know It’s Christmas?”, recorded in 1984 with voices including George Michael, Boy George and Bono. This is the original recording, rather than one of the later versions, and a significant moment in music fundraising.

pages.before: Band Aid is a charity supergroup featuring mainly British and Irish musicians and recording artists.

records.after: Kelly Clarkson’s American Idol breakthrough led to a pop career that includes “Since U Been Gone” and “Stronger”. Her Christmas album Wrapped in Red introduced “Underneath the Tree”, co-written with Greg Kurstin. It puts her powerful voice at the centre of a busy, joyful arrangement, making a convincing case for company over anything wrapped in a box.

pages.before: Kelly Brianne Clarkson is an American singer, songwriter, author, and occasional actress. She rose to fame in 2002 after winning the inaugural season of American Idol, and has since been referred to as the "Original American Idol

Kelly Clarkson is celebrating Christmas with a new single, Christmas Isn’t Canceled (Just You). The song heralds her ninth studio album, When Christmas Comes Around, out October 15th via Atlantic Records.

records.after: Chris Rea combined a distinctive, weathered voice with blues-influenced guitar playing on songs such as “The Road to Hell”. “Driving Home for Christmas” finds him on a rather more welcoming journey. Its unhurried rhythm and everyday observations capture the anticipation of getting back to familiar faces, even when the journey itself takes a little patience.

pages.before: Christopher Anton Rea is an English singer-songwriter and guitarist, recognisable for his distinctive, husky voice and slide guitar playing.

records.after: Ariana Grande moved from television into a pop career built on expressive vocals and songs including “Problem” and “Thank U, Next”. Her Christmas Kisses EP includes a fresh take on Wham!’s “Last Christmas”. It brings her own vocal character to a familiar seasonal story, rather than simply following the original recording note for note.

pages.before: Ariana Grande-Butera, known professionally as Ariana Grande, is an American singer and actress. She began her career in the Broadway musical 13, before landing the role of Cat Valentine on the Nickelodeon television series Victorious in 2009

Ariana Grande-Butera is an American singer, songwriter, and actress. Her four-octave vocal range has received critical acclaim, and her personal life has been the subject of widespread media attention.

records.after: Bastille broke through with “Pompeii”, combining Dan Smith’s distinctive voice with a chorus built for communal singing. Their version of Slade’s “Merry Xmas Everybody” brings a familiar Christmas favourite into the band’s repertoire. It’s a chance to hear those well-known words through a different pop voice, while keeping the invitation to join in firmly intact.

pages.before: Bastille are an English pop rock band formed in 2010. The group began as a solo project by lead vocalist Dan Smith, but later expanded to include keyboardist Kyle Simmons, bassist and guitarist Will Farquarson and drummer Chris "Woody" Wood.

records.after: Dido’s quietly distinctive voice helped make No Angel a breakthrough album, with songs including “Thank You” and “Here with Me”. “Christmas Day” offers a story-led seasonal recording rather than a party anthem. Its wintry atmosphere makes a gentle contrast to the bigger choruses around it, inviting you to listen closely for a few minutes.

pages.before: Dido Florian Cloud de Bounevialle O'Malley Armstrong, known as Dido, is an English singer and songwriter. Dido attained international success with her debut album No Angel.

records.after: Carly Rae Jepsen’s “Call Me Maybe” introduced her to a worldwide audience, while albums such as Emotion showed the breadth of her pop songwriting. Her festive song “It’s Not Christmas Till Somebody Cries” takes a wry look at imperfect celebrations. A useful reminder that a family Christmas needn’t resemble a glossy advert to be memorable.

pages.before: Carly Rae Jepsen is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and actress. In 2007, she placed third in Canadian Idol season five's competition. Jepsen independently released her debut album, Tug of War, in 2008.

pages.song: It's Not Christmas Till Somebody Cries
pages.before: Carly Rae Jepsen is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and actress. Born and raised in Mission, British Columbia, Jepsen performed several lead roles in her high school's musical productions and pursued musical theatre at the Canadian College of Performing Arts in Victoria, BC.

records.after: Darlene Love’s voice is at the heart of “Christmas (Baby Please Come Home)”, a recording that balances longing with a rush of energy. Her wider career includes 1960s singles such as “(Today I Met) The Boy I’m Gonna Marry”. At Christmas, that expressive delivery gives even the biggest arrangement a wonderfully human centre.

pages.before: Darlene Love is an American popular music singer and actress. She gained prominence in the 1960s for the song "He's a Rebel," a No. 1 American single in 1962, and was one of the artists who performed on the celebrated Christmas album A Christmas Gift for You from Phil Spector.

records.after: Coldplay grew from the intimate appeal of “Yellow” into a band associated with expansive songs and communal choruses. Their 2010 single “Christmas Lights” begins in a more troubled mood before opening into hope. It’s a seasonal song that makes room for mixed feelings, with Chris Martin’s voice guiding the move from reflection towards celebration.

pages.before: Coldplay are a British rock band formed in 1996 by lead vocalist and keyboardist Chris Martin and lead guitarist Jonny Buckland at University College London.

records.after: Ed Sheeran and Elton John bring two generations of British songwriting together on “Merry Christmas”. Released in 2021, their duet reached number one in the UK. Elton’s piano-pop tradition and Ed’s melodic storytelling meet in a song made for sharing, with enough bells and good cheer to make the title feel entirely appropriate.

records.after: East 17 brought a streetwise pop sound to the 1990s, with songs including “House of Love” and “It’s Alright”. Their ballad “Stay Another Day” became the UK Christmas number one in 1994. It wasn’t originally written as a Christmas song, but those bells and the snowy video helped give it a lasting December home.

pages.before: East 17 are an English pop boy band group currently consisting of original members John Hendy and Terry Coldwell and newest addition to the line-up Robbie Craig. The original line-up also featured Brian Harvey and Tony Mortimer.

records.after: Shakin’ Stevens brought rock ’n’ roll style to the British pop charts with hits such as “This Ole House” and “Oh Julie”. “Merry Christmas Everyone” became the UK Christmas number one in 1985. Its cheerful bounce makes it a natural party choice, even for anyone whose dancing is usually confined to avoiding the wrapping paper.

pages.before: Michael Barratt, known as Shakin Stevens, is a platinum-selling Welsh rock and roll singer and songwriter who was the UK's biggest-selling singles artist of the 1980s.
Michael Barratt, known as Shakin Stevens, is a platinum-selling Welsh rock and roll singer and songwriter who was the UK's biggest-selling singles artist of the 1980s.

records.after: Elvis Presley brought rock ’n’ roll, country and blues into a distinctive musical mix, alongside a gift for heartfelt ballads. His Christmas recordings show both sides, from lively seasonal songs to the yearning “Blue Christmas”. That familiar voice gives the festive repertoire character without needing every song to turn into a full-scale celebration.

records.after: Sia built a career as both a distinctive singer and a songwriter for other artists, with “Chandelier” becoming one of her signature songs. Everyday Is Christmas brings her melodic instincts to original seasonal material, including “Santa’s Coming for Us”.
